text: Weeks of building and testing have left the usual residue in Fairmont's Azure subscription: a few unattached disks, an untagged public IP, the normal drift nobody notices until a cost review asks why.
This video builds the fix as routine automation: a PowerShell runbook, running weekly inside Azure Automation under its own scoped managed identity.
It queries the subscription with Azure Resource Graph for untagged resources and disks sitting unattached for more than a week — one query, across everything, every week.
It defaults to a dry-run report — nothing gets deleted automatically. The first real run turns up two leftover test disks and one untagged IP, reviewed and cleared by hand.
Routine ops, closed the same way the credential work was: scoped, automated, and reviewed before anything irreversible happens. The infrastructure is live — next, harvest actually hits it.
